passages.literalWordingSummary: One Firewood token is listed. Component count is not a Rest completion rule.
Set the Firewood token beside Provisions. Does not govern spending or completion.
The Quest identifies Firewood supplies and the top-left Resting Point amount; take its Firewood token into Provisions.
Food/Bandage/Potion effects are Provision effects; they do not define unused Resting Points.

Rest requires a cleared Room and party agreement. Collectively distribute the Quest amount, recover one Life or one Stress per point spent, allow equal split if agreement fails, then discard Firewood after Rest. No all-points, unused-points, or insufficient-capacity completion instruction is stated.
Healing removes Wound tokens. This bounds actual removal by tokens present; it does not require rejecting an oversized Rest allocation.
Critical healing and Stress recovery are combat effects, not Rest completion authority.
Recovering Stress decreases its tracked value. Does not define legal spending without recovery.
A won Battle clears the Room and the party can Rest there.
Fast Healer and Resilient modify healing/recovery. They do not establish an all-points or unused-Rest-points rule. Frozen Hero behavior is not re-reviewed.
Stress starts at zero and is tracked up to ten. The physical track is context for bounded recovery, not a Rest allocation rejection rule.
Healing removes Wounds and can end Death’s Door; the Wound ceiling is not a Rest spend requirement.
Face the Threat provides Firewood; the illustrated Quest shows 12 points. Boss setup is not standard Rest completion authority.
Unused Provisions are returned for Gold on returning to Hamlet. This is not disposal of unspent Resting Points during Rest.
Hamlet building visits allow recovery; they do not govern Dungeon Resting Points.

Recovery in the Hamlet is distinct from Dungeon Rest.

corpusConclusion: Reviewed all ten locked rulebook/tutorial files, existing core extracts and the 76 printed Quest bindings. No official instruction settles full-budget completion or insufficient recovery capacity. Search absence alone is not the conclusion: Rest passages and recovery context were reviewed, with exceptions confined to their printed scope.
printedBudgetBasis: Printed Quest budget/icons bound by Core p11 and frozen C4A. A printed dash is zero budget; token count is a derived setup fact. Transport identifiers are locators only. Lowercase remaining-room/Monster references to the rest do not instruct a Rest action.
